paragraphs.text: Pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndrome-8 (PPGL8) is a tumor predisposition caused by germline TMEM127 mutation. Affected individuals mainly develop pheochromocytomas, catecholamine-secreting tumors of the adrenal medulla, which are bilateral in a substantial proportion of patients and usually arise at ages similar to those of sporadic pheochromocytoma (Qin et al., 2010; Yao et al., 2010). Paragangliomas and renal cell carcinoma have also been reported in carriers, and metastatic disease is rare (Armaiz-Pena et al., 2021).

paragraphs.text: Qin et al. (2010) reported 7 index patients and families with germline TMEM127 mutations. In family 1, 7 sibs were affected, with a total of 10 tumors and age at onset ranging from 34 to 54 years; 3 of the 7 had bilateral tumors. Across the series, patients developed pheochromocytomas at a mean age of 45.3 years, similar to the mean age at diagnosis of sporadic pheochromocytomas (43.6 to 43.9 years) but older than syndromic cases (24.9 to 30.2 years). All tumors arose from the adrenal medulla and were bilateral in approximately half of the patients. No malignancies, defined as metastasis to nonchromaffin tissues, or recurrences were detected during follow-up of 4 to 16 years. Four mutation carriers in family 1 remained without clinical disease at ages 43 to 58 years.

paragraphs.text: Toledo et al. (2015) studied a 6-generation family carrying a germline TMEM127 mutation. Clinical data were available for 34 mutation carriers followed for 8.7 +/- 8.1 years (range, 1 to 20 years). Pheochromocytoma was diagnosed in 11 carriers (32%) at a median age of 43 years. In 9 patients symptoms began at a median of 29 years (range, 10 to 55 years), and 2 were asymptomatic. Tumors were multicentric in 5 (45%) and bilateral in 5 (45%) patients, and 6 patients (54%) had at least 1 adrenomedullary nodule less than 10 mm. No paragangliomas, distant metastases, or other manifestations were found. Cumulative penetrance of pheochromocytoma was 0% at 0 to 20 years, 3% at 21 to 30 years, 15% at 31 to 40 years, 24% at 41 to 50 years, and 32% at 51 to 65 years. The youngest patient was diagnosed at 22 years, and the earliest symptoms were reported at age 10. The authors noted tumor multicentricity, nodular adrenomedullary hyperplasia, and onset of symptoms more than a decade before diagnosis as novel features.

Imaging showed a 4 x 4 x 6-cm mass in the left supraclavicular fossa, confirmed as a paraganglioma by MIBG scintigraphy and histology; plasma free metanephrines were normal. She also had acromegaly due to a 13-mm growth hormone-secreting pituitary macroadenoma. Her medical and family history was otherwise unremarkable apart from multinodular goiter. Both tumors were cured by surgery, and she remained well after 10 years of follow-up. The authors attributed the hypertensive episodes to the acromegaly.

paragraphs.text: In a family with familial pheochromocytoma, Dahia et al. (2005) found identical multipoint parametric lod scores of 2.97 for loci at chromosome 2cen and 16p13. Two-locus parametric linkage analysis gave a maximum lod score of 5.16 under a double recessive multiplicative model, suggesting that both loci were required for disease. Allele-specific loss of heterozygosity (LOH) was detected only at the chromosome 2 locus in all tumors from the family, consistent with a tumor suppressor gene. (2010) identified a heterozygous germline splice site mutation in the TMEM127 gene (IVS3-2A-C), predicted to result in a frameshift (Leu138fs) and a 148-amino acid protein. The mutation was absent from 2 unaffected sibs; 4 mutation carriers remained unaffected at ages 43 to 58 years. The same mutation was found in a second family (family 5) with 2 affected individuals, and haplotype analysis excluded a common ancestor. The mutation was not found in 1,064 control alleles, and tumors showed loss of the wildtype allele.

agent.process_note: Read all 9 papers in full as available: Qin et al. (2010) and Stutz et al. (2020) are full texts; the other 7 are abstracts only, and I used only what each abstract states. I searched for ancestry, ethnicity and consanguinity; the only ancestry statements were Japanese patients and a 'Brazilian case' in Takeichi et al. Qin et al. give no ancestry for their families. No gene MIM number or HGNC reference data were supplied, so the intro omits the gene MIM number; the 2q11 location is taken from Qin et al. Toledo's c.410-2A>C and Qin's IVS3-2A>C may be the same change, and Takeichi's c.116_119delTGTC and Delgado's c.117_120delGTCT may be equivalent. The papers do not say so, so I kept them as separate variants. The c.245-10C>G variant of Stutz et al. is a VUS and was not listed as an allelic variant. Dahia et al. (2005) proposed digenic inheritance, which conflicts with the later dominant model of Qin et al. Both views are described.
